title: 28-year-old Keizer man gets 11 years in federal prison for trafficking fentanyl, meth - NewsBreak
text: A Keizer man was sentenced July 30 to more than 11 years in federal prison for trafficking more than 17 pounds of fentanyl and methamphetamine in Oregon and Washington. Caden Jay Christman, 28, was arrested in Montana in February 2024 after police seized 9 pounds of methamphetamine, more than 5,000 fentanyl pills, about $17,000 in cash and two loaded firearms from his vehicle during a traffic stop, according to the U.S. Attorney's Office District of Oregon. Police had been tracking Christman and a co-defendant as they traveled from Keizer, through Washington and into Montana, according to a sentencing memorandum. Police conducted search warrants of Christman's home in Keizer and seized 15,000 fentanyl pills, 4 pounds of fentanyl powder, 2 pounds of methamphetamine, heroin, $21,600 in cash and 12 firearms. Christman was indicted on charges of possession with intent to distribute fentanyl, methamphetamine, and heroin, and possession of a firearm in furtherance of a drug trafficking crime. He pleaded guilty in February to possession with intent to distribute fentanyl. Isabel Funk covers breaking news and public safety for the Statesman Journal. Funk can be reached at ifunk@statesmanjournal.com or on X at @isabeldfunk This article originally appeared on Salem Statesman Journal: 28-year-old Keizer man gets 11 years in federal prison for trafficking fentanyl, meth
